visuals.title: Quiz
visuals.text: Five questions. Answer along on the cards below the transcript, then hear Marco's answers.

quiz.pause_at: Pause here if you want to think it through

questions.q: Enterprise value 600, EBITDA 50. What's the EV / EBITDA multiple?
questions.explain: 600 ÷ 50 = 12x: roughly, the market is paying twelve years of today's EBITDA.
questions.explain_at: Value divided by a financial metric

questions.q: Comparable companies trade at 8x EBITDA. Your target has EBITDA of 40 and net debt of 100. What's its implied equity value?
questions.explain: 8 × 40 = 320 of enterprise value; subtract 100 of net debt for 220 of equity value. 320 is the EV, not equity.
questions.explain_at: That's literally how a comps valuation works

questions.q: A company has negative EBITDA. Which multiple would you use?
questions.explain: With negative EBITDA there's no meaningful EBITDA multiple, so use revenue, remembering it ignores differences in margins.
questions.explain_at: When EBITDA is negative or tiny

questions.q: Share price 30, earnings per share 2. What's the P/E?
questions.explain: P/E is share price over earnings per share: 30 ÷ 2 = 15x.
questions.explain_at: And price over earnings, the P-E ratio

questions.q: Enterprise value 1,200, last year's EBITDA 100, next year's 120. Trailing and forward multiples?
questions.explain: 1,200 ÷ 100 = 12x on last year; 1,200 ÷ 120 = 10x on next year. Growing EBITDA makes the forward multiple lower.
questions.explain_at: For a growing company, the forward multiple is lower
